title: Temperature Sensors - Comparing Types
description: Comparing advantages and disadvantages of thermocouples, RTDs and thermistors temperature sensors.

components.content:
## Temperature Sensors Comparison

This tool compares three main types of temperature sensors:

### Thermocouple
A thermocouple has two dissimilar conductors forming electrical junctions at differing temperatures. The thermocouple produces a temperature-dependent voltage as a result of the thermoelectric effect and can be interpreted as a temperature measurement.

### RTD (Resistance Thermometer Detector)
RTDs are made of a length of fine wire wrapped around a ceramic or glass core. The RTD wire is of pure material - typically platinum, nickel, or copper - with an accurate resistance/temperature relationship. The electrical resistance provides an indication of the temperature.

### Thermistor
A thermistor is a type of resistor made of ceramic or polymer materials. The resistance is - like the RTD - dependent on temperature. A PTC (Positive Temperature Coefficient) conducts better at lower temperatures. A NTC (Negative Temperature Coefficient) conducts better at higher temperatures.
